what_i_see: A bright, smooth, red elliptical with a bright core and extended round halo (~10 arcsec) dominates the field, surrounded by small faint galaxies. About 6 arcsec NW of its centre lies a faint, slightly curved, roughly tangential smudge, visible mainly in the enlarged VIS panel. No tidal features, dust lanes or obvious counter-images.
most_likely: A luminous early-type galaxy at z_phot ~0.24, probably in a group linked to WHL J100159.4+662739 (same z, 77 arcsec away). The faint curved feature is most likely a small background galaxy seen at low S/N.
against_it: The faint feature is curved and roughly tangential at ~6 arcsec, so a weak group-scale lensed arc cannot be excluded. There is no counter-image, and the feature has too little S/N to judge.
decisive_test: Deeper or PSF-subtracted VIS imaging with a galaxy-light model removed, looking for a counter-image opposite the arc; or a spectroscopic redshift of the arc above the lens redshift.
catalogue_notes: SDSS J100212.42+662710.9 (r=17.8, zph 0.243), with Gaia/AllWISE/2MASS counterparts at 5.85 arcsec SE of the given position. Clusters WHL J100159.4+662739 (zph 0.233) at 77 arcsec and Wen+2024 J100157.7+662631 (z 0.43) at ~85 arcsec. No SIMBAD object within 150 arcsec.
